large_guidance:
- Restructure so each program emits one pooled output `(n, c, dp, hp, wp)` with `BLOCK_W` covering only the 2 W-elements per pool window — but since LayerNorm reduces across W, keep one program per `(n, c, dp, hp)` row and produce all `Wp` outputs. After the 2x2 (dd,hh) accumulation into `acc[BLOCK_W]`, compute pooled outputs as `pooled[wp] = acc[2*wp] + acc[2*wp+1]` using two strided loads of `acc` via index gather (`tl.arange(0, half)*2` and `*2+1`) or by maintaining two parallel accumulators of length `half` from the start (mask-select even/odd lanes during the dd/hh inner loop).
- Alternative cleaner design: make `BLOCK_W` cover `Wp` lanes; inside loops, for each lane load `x[2*wp]` and `x[2*wp+1]` separately, sum them, then run LayerNorm across the full W dimension with a separate pre-pass tile. Two-pass (mean/var first, then normalize+pool) inside one kernel avoids any reshape gymnastics.
- Ensure correctness: LayerNorm normalizes over the last dim of size `norm_shape[0]=C=64` in the reference (since `norm_shape=(out_channels,)` and ConvTranspose3d output has C as dim 1) — verify which axis is normalized; the current kernel normalizes over W, which may be wrong. LayerNorm with `normalized_shape=(C,)` applies to the last dim of the input, but PyTorch's LayerNorm normalizes over the trailing dims matching `normalized_shape`. Since input is `(N,C,D,H,W)` and norm_shape is `(64,)=C`, it would try to normalize over W (size 32), which mismatches — actually PyTorch will error unless W==64. Re-examine the reference shape contract before redesigning.
